system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The Seller’s “FINAL”, agreed-bargain and market-standard assertions are not evidence of Buyer approval. The positions below are based only on the supplied extracts; the underlying SPA and DD records require verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher cap, reflecting diligence findings, available recourse and insurance, with separate regimes for other claim categories. | **Counter with a higher cap; do not accept 20% as settled** — recoverable losses could materially exceed AUD 4.8m. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Each claim must exceed **AUD 25,000**; aggregate claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, aggregation of related claims, and exclusions for fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims. | **Reduce thresholds and replace the deductible basket with a tipping basket** — the proposed combination leaves substantial losses with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations presumptively extend to all Claims. | **24–36 months** for general warranties; separate category-specific periods; timely notified claims survive until resolved. | **Seek a longer general period and delete universal application** — latent issues may emerge after 18 months and other claims need distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and deadline. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; at least a purchase-price cap and substantially longer survival. | **Reject treatment as general warranties** — defective ownership threatens the entire acquisition, not merely part of its value. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions cover all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent concealment claims and remedies, outside contractual caps, thresholds, deadlines, disclosure and knowledge defences. | **Insert an overriding fraud carve-out across all relevant provisions** — Seller must not use contractual limitations to shelter fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; specific warranty references and a frozen, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and tightly define fair disclosure** — document availability alone does not explain a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without constructive knowledge, adviser imputation or duty to enquire. | **Delete, or narrowly confine, the qualifier and exclude specific indemnities** — discoverability would shift extensive undiscovered risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although final consent and evidence of associated conditions are absent. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring valid consent and satisfaction of contractual conditions, without materially adverse amendments or charges. | **Require substantive satisfaction before Completion, with a long-stop termination right** — a document alone may not protect a customer representing approximately 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout figures, repayment through the completion funds flow, effective release of security and guarantees at Completion, and correct debt adjustment. | **Make repayment and release simultaneous completion deliverables, supported by binding lender arrangements** — Buyer should not acquire an encumbered business or fund debt twice. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses are omitted from funds flow; on-cost treatment unknown. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with payment mechanics and employee entitlements verified. | **Include the full liability in agreed price/funds-flow mechanics and obtain residual protection, without double counting** — omission could leave Buyer funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without verified payment or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective IP vesting/assignment before Completion, plus protection against pre-Completion ownership defects, claims and remediation costs. | **Require the IP cure and broaden the specific indemnity beyond the invoice amount** — paying the outstanding fee alone may not establish complete ownership or cover resulting losses. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational issue, said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt forensic and legal investigation, evidence preservation, containment, required notifications and a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident consequences, to the extent lawful. | **Keep the issue open pending findings and negotiate dedicated protection/security** — uncertainty is neither proof of a reportable breach nor a basis to dismiss exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. | Aggregate assessment of timing, scope, cancellation rights, accruals and commercial necessity, plus appropriate pre-Completion covenant and price treatment. | **Investigate the AUD 330,000 package before classifying it; seek adjustment or protection if warranted** — neither “ordinary course” nor debt-like treatment is established by the extracts. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly displaced. | Clearly distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, payment/adjustment obligations, covenants and fraud. | **Add express exclusions and a precedence clause throughout the SPA** — omnibus wording could silently defeat separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Seller as 100% holder. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital, historical allotments/transfers, certificates, constitution, options/convertibles, encumbrances and third-party rights; effective transfer deliverables. | **Complete title diligence and require clean-title warranties and completion documents** — a register entry alone does not establish unencumbered ownership of the entire equity. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties considered settled within the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with appropriate statutory-period protection; robust IP ownership, licensing, infringement and contractor-assignment warranties plus known-risk indemnities. | **Reopen tax and IP expressly, with tailored caps, periods and exclusions** — long-tail tax exposure and core SaaS IP risk should not default to the general 20%/18-month regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
